statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail stays low with equity index futures closed and no live NQ price path, while Stress rises to elevated because Friday's risk-on close was priced on a Strait of Hormuz reopening deal that was rejected over the weekend.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. A narrow danger window is published from the Sunday 22:00Z CME futures reopen into the early Asian hours, where the unpriced weekend escalation would first be expressed in price. Existing-position management and emergency protection logic are unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 Tail low into the Sunday reopen; Stress rises as the weekend reverses Friday's Hormuz-deal optimism
body: Equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00Z, so no live NQ price path exists at this assessment time and the current Tail reading reflects absent path risk rather than an observed benign trend. Friday's verified cash close was orderly: the Nasdaq-100 finished at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, mid-range inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 day range and about half a percent below its 30,770.63 52-week high, with the Nasdaq Composite at 27,068.72 up 0.48%, the S&P 500 at 7,743.41 and VIX down 5.11% to 14.87. That combination shows no shallow-pullback extension, no holding of session extremes and no repeated failure of retracement, which is the evidence the Tail contract requires before a higher reading is justified. The material weekend change is why Stress rises rather than holds. Friday's reporting attributed the equity gains and a 2.33% oil decline directly to optimism over a possible deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, part of a discussed phased US-Iran arrangement. On Saturday that specific deal was rejected: Iran's seven-day proposal to reopen the strait, resume nuclear talks and reduce hostilities in exchange for lifting the US naval blockade, releasing about $12 billion in frozen assets and easing oil sanctions was declined as not acceptable, with a claim of total US control over the waterway. Escalation then widened on Sunday, with US measures targeting Iran's aviation sector, several countries suspending Iranian airline flights, and Saudi Arabia pressing for international support on freedom of navigation, while Iran's foreign minister said Tehran awaited an official response through mediators. The specific premise underlying Friday's risk-on close has therefore been weakened while no market was open to reprice it, which concentrates gap and repricing risk at the Sunday 22:00Z futures reopen. Under the risk contract that is a Stress and Confidence input, not present Tail evidence: an unpriced catalyst is not observed price-path failure, and a reopen gap only becomes a Tail amplifier if it is followed by shallow or failed retracements and repeated extension. The rates backdrop is unchanged and demanding. H.15 shows the 2-year at 4.87%, the 10-year at 5.18% and the 30-year at 5.47%, with the 10-year near its highest in about two decades, while markets price roughly a 66% chance of an October Fed hike and 52% for December against firm activity data including 3.4% annualised Q2 real consumer spending and August payrolls of 162,000. WTI settled at $92.41, down 2.33% on Friday and about 7.4% on the week, with Brent near $104.32, and conflict transmission is visible in record $6.48 diesel and $4.48 gasoline. Those conditions describe a difficult, potentially high-drawdown environment that can still mean-revert, which maps to elevated Stress rather than to Tail. The shared Finviz context read this run was partial, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, and its breadth and megacap figures are labeled latest-session and non-real-time, so it was used only as background and not to establish current structure; that background showed an internally split tape with Technology up 0.85% and semiconductors firm against Communication Services down 0.58%. Confidence holds in the solid band: index levels, yields, oil, VIX, the weekend Iran developments and the full week-ahead calendar were verified from primary and reputable current sources this run, but the live NQ price path remains unavailable until futures reopen at 22:00Z, and the last observed path was set under a de-escalation assumption that the weekend has undercut.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots are available from published Claude assessments and were left unchanged. Tail drifted from 8 down to 6 across the period while Stress rose from 47 to 58 and Confidence decayed from 83 to 67, reflecting an orderly Friday cash session followed by a weekend with no live price discovery and an increasingly demanding rates and oil backdrop. The mapped state remained EA_ON throughout.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail in the low band across all 24 hours. Risk is held near the closed-period baseline through Sunday, lifts into a published danger window at the 22:00Z CME equity index futures reopen where the unpriced weekend Hormuz escalation would first be expressed in price, and then decays through the Asian hours on the assumption that reopen pricing is absorbed with normal two-way discovery rather than one-way extension. That assumption is explicitly untested; observed shallow or failed retracements after the reopen would be the evidence to reassess upward. Confidence improves materially after the reopen because a live NQ price path becomes observable again. Stress stays high through the reopen and eases only to elevated, because a two-decade-high long end, elevated oil and an unresolved Hormuz conflict persist into a data-heavy week running from JOLTS and consumer confidence on Sep 29 through August Core PCE on Sep 30, ISM Manufacturing on Oct 1 and September payrolls on Oct 2.
